# Widows and orphans

This file holds paragraphs of many different lengths, from one short sentence to a dozen, so that at almost any page height and column width some paragraph straddles a page boundary. Each section ends with a heading that sits close to the next block, to exercise keep with next.

## One line

A single short line.

## Two lines

A paragraph that needs two lines, no more, and which must never be split between pages because it is far too short to leave two lines on each side.

## Three lines

The lighthouse keeper wrote the same sentence in his log every evening: the wind was from the west, the sea was calm, and the lamp was lit before the last light left the water. On some evenings he added a second sentence about the gulls.

## Four lines

When the ferry finally arrived the whole village was waiting on the quay, wrapped in coats, holding baskets and lanterns and the small paper flags the children had folded that afternoon. Nobody spoke while the ropes were thrown, and then everybody spoke at once, which is how it always goes when someone comes home after a long time away, carrying more news than any one conversation can hold.

## Five lines

The map on the wall was older than anyone in the house. Its coastlines were drawn with a confidence that the survey of later years had quietly corrected, and its inland rivers ran where somebody had wished them to run. Even so, the grandmother used it to explain the way to the market, the way to the church, and the way to the field where the first apple tree had been planted by a man whose name nobody remembered. She tapped the paper with one finger at every turning, and her listeners nodded as if the route were obvious, though most of them would take the long way round anyway.

## Six lines

Learning to bind a book by hand begins with patience and a good bone folder. The sheets are folded, nested into small groups, and pressed under a weight overnight so that the paper forgets its flatness. Then comes the sewing: a curved needle, waxed thread, and a rhythm of in and out along the spine that the hands learn long before the mind can describe it. Each group is tied to the one before with a small knot, and the knots must lie flat or the cover will bulge. When the last group is attached, the spine is glued, clamped, and left alone for a day, which is the hardest part for anyone who wants to see the result.

Seven lines of text follow, written so that the paragraph is long enough to be split in the middle but short enough that a bad break would leave one stranded line at either end of the split. The tinker walked slowly up the hill with his sack of pots, stopping at every gate to ask whether anything needed mending, and at each gate the answer was a polite no, until the last house, where a woman in a green apron held out a kettle with a hole in the bottom and told him the story of how it had been dented in a flood. He listened to all of it, nodded, turned the kettle over twice, and said that it would take an hour, which was a lie, since he could do it in ten minutes, but it was a good lie because it earned him a seat by the fire and a cup of something hot.

### Heading level three before a short paragraph

Short.

### Heading level three before a two line paragraph

Two lines would be the least a heading may carry along with it to the next page, so this paragraph is written to be just about that long and not a word longer than that.

#### Two headings in a row

##### Directly after another heading

The paragraph under stacked headings must travel with both of them, which makes the whole group tall, and the group must still be placed by the same rule as any other heading.

## A list that crosses pages

- The first item is a single short line.
- The second item is longer and runs over to a second line because it carries a little more detail than the one before it, enough to wrap at a narrow width.
- The third item is the longest of the group. It describes a small procedure in prose: take the flat sheet, fold it once along the grain, crease it firmly with the side of the thumb, and set it aside with the others until the stack is tall enough to sew.
- Fourth.
- Fifth, with a little text.
- Sixth is short as well.

> A quotation can also cross a page boundary. The left rule has to stay continuous on both sides of the break, and the lines of the quotation obey the same rule about leaving two lines behind and two lines ahead, no matter how long the quotation turns out to be when it is set at a narrow width in a large type size.

The end.
